crawford1814.summary: Crawford reports to Monroe, in code, his belief that the French government has resolved to sacrifice everything for England's friendship and that the King looks to British troops in Belgium for protection against his own people; a reported conspiracy headed by Savary, which opponents call a police fabrication to justify about thirty arrests; a coming crisis for the King, with many expecting the royal family to be expelled again; and three parties if there is a struggle: the army for the Emperor, part of the new nobility for the King of Rome with a regency or for the Duke of Orleans, and the republicans with either of the last two.
crawford1814.en:
I am inclined to believe that this government has come to a determination to sacrifice every thing for the
friendship of England. The use of the Telegraphs has been granted to Lord Wellington, to enable him to ascertain with
the greatest dispatch what passes in Belgium. The King, so far from viewing with an eye of jealousy the augmentation
of British troops [and] others in British pay in that country, looks to that force for protection against his own
people. It is reported and believed that a conspiracy has been discovered, at the head of which they have placed
Savary. Those opposed to the government [say] that this [conspiracy] is the creature of the police, fabricated to
countenance the arrest of about thirty persons, of whom the court is afraid. [A] report also prevails to day that the
discussions at Vienna have assumed a hostile tone [...]

[...]

system: The State Department's numerical code of about 1,600 words and syllables that Weber (1979) prints as WE025 (the = 1355, of = 1397, to = 1554), Poinsett's 'code 1355'; marks on the groups for -s, -ed, dropped and doubled letters, as the code's own directions…
